text: Who was the Viceroy of India when the Quit India Movement started in 1942?
explanation: Lord Linlithgow was the longest-serving Viceroy (1936–1943) and oversaw the start of the movement and WWII mobilization in India.

text: The 'Article 360' of the Indian Constitution is related to?
explanation: Financial Emergency has never been declared in India so far.

text: Which of these rivers is a tributary of the Godavari?
explanation: Pranhita is the largest tributary of Godavari. Koyna and Bhima are tributaries of the Krishna river.

text: Who was the first Indian to receive the 'Bharat Ratna'?
explanation: In 1954, the first three recipients were Rajagopalachari, Radhakrishnan, and C.V. Raman.

text: Which state has the lowest population density in India as per 2011 Census?
explanation: Arunachal Pradesh has a density of only 17 persons per square kilometer.

text: Which schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with 'Anti-Defection Law'?
explanation: The 10th Schedule was added by the 52nd Amendment Act in 1985.

text: The 'Battle of Haldighati' (1576) was fought between Maharana Pratap and?
explanation: Maharana Pratap of Mewar fought against the Mughal forces led by Raja Man Singh of Amber.

text: Which is the most abundant gas in the Earth's atmosphere?
explanation: Nitrogen makes up approximately 78% of the dry atmosphere, followed by Oxygen at 21%.

text: Who is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
explanation: The Vice-President presides over the Upper House of Parliament.

text: The 'Grand Canyon' is located along which river?
explanation: The Colorado River carved the Grand Canyon in Arizona, USA, over millions of years.

text: 'Bull' and 'Bear' terms are associated with which activity?
explanation: A Bull market is rising; a Bear market is falling.

text: What is 'SLR' in banking terms?
explanation: SLR is the minimum percentage of deposits that a commercial bank has to maintain in the form of liquid assets (Cash, Gold, etc.).

text: Who regulates the 'Capital Market' in India?
explanation: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) is the regulator for securities and commodity markets.

text: What is the full form of 'NEFT'?
explanation: NEFT is a nationwide payment system facilitating one-to-one funds transfer.

text: In banking, what does 'KYC' stand for?
explanation: KYC is a process to verify the identity and address of customers to prevent money laundering.

text: Which was the first metal used by man?
explanation: Copper was the first metal to be used, during the Chalcolithic age (Copper-Stone age).

text: Who among the following was the political guru of Mahatma Gandhi?
explanation: Gokhale advised Gandhi to spend its initial years traveling across India to understand its people and problems.

text: Which is the highest peak in the Western Ghats?
explanation: Anamudi (Kerala) is the highest peak in both the Western Ghats and South India.

text: How many languages are listed in the 8th Schedule of the Indian Constitution?
explanation: Originally there were 14, now there are 22 official languages recognized by the schedule.

text: Which city is known as the 'Electronic City of India'?
explanation: Bengaluru is the hub of India's IT and electronic industries.

text: Who is known as the 'Frontier Gandhi'?
explanation: He founded the 'Khudai Khidmatgar' and was a pacifist leader in the North-West Frontier Province.

text: The 'Palk Strait' separates India from which country?
explanation: It is an inlet of the Bay of Bengal between Tamil Nadu and the Jaffna District of Sri Lanka.

text: Which organ of the human body produces 'Insulin'?
explanation: The islets of Langerhans in the pancreas secrete insulin to regulate blood sugar levels.

text: The 'Lothal' dockyard of the Indus Valley Civilization is located in which state?
explanation: Lothal (Gujarat) was one of the most prominent cities of the IVC, serving as a vital port.

text: Who was the first Governor-General of Bengal?
explanation: Warren Hastings became the first Governor-General under the Regulating Act of 1773.

text: What is 'Call Money' in the banking industry?
option_a: Loan given to customers on call
option_b: Short-term finance repayable on demand, with maturity period of 1 to 14 days
option_c: Calling a customer to pay their loan
explanation: It's used by banks for inter-bank transactions to maintain their CRR/SLR.

text: Which of these is NOT a 'Public Sector Bank'?
explanation: HDFC and ICICI are private sector banks, unlike SBI which is government-owned.

text: What is 'Fiscal Deficit'?
option_a: The difference between government's total expenditure and its total receipts excluding borrowing
option_b: The total amount of money in the bank
option_c: The salary of the finance minister
option_d: The cost of building a new office
explanation: It indicates the total borrowing requirements of the government from all sources.

text: Which institution provides 'Crop Insurance' to farmers in India?
explanation: AIC implements various insurance schemes to protect farmers from climate and crop loss.

text: The 'Repo Rate' is the rate at which?
option_b: RBI lends money to commercial banks
explanation: It's the main tool of RBI's monetary policy to control inflation and money supply.

text: Who built the 'Grand Trunk Road' (GT Road)?
explanation: Sher Shah Suri renovated and extended this ancient route connecting Kabul to Chittagong.

text: Which is the largest organ in the human body?
explanation: The skin is both an organ and the largest tissue system covering the entire body.

text: What is the minimum age to be eligible for the Lok Sabha elections?
explanation: 25 years for Lok Sabha; 30 years for Rajya Sabha; 35 years for President.

text: In which city was the 'Azad Hind Fauj' (INA) founded?
explanation: It was initially founded by Mohan Singh in Singapore in 1942, then later led by Subhas Chandra Bose.

text: Which is the most literate state of India as per 2011 census?
explanation: Kerala has nearly 94% literacy rate.

text: Who was the last Mughal Emperor of India?
explanation: He was the titular leader of the 1857 revolt and was later deported to Rangoon by the British.

text: Which chemical name is 'Plaster of Paris'?
explanation: Its chemical formula is CaSO4·1/2H2O.

text: Which ocean is 'S-shaped'?
explanation: The Atlantic Ocean lies between Europe/Africa and the Americas, forming an S-shape.

text: Who was the 'Rani of Jhansi' during 1857 revolt?
explanation: She led the revolt in Jhansi after the British refused to recognize her adopted son's right to the throne.

text: The 'Mount Everest' is also known as what in Nepal?
explanation: In Nepal, it's called Sagarmatha (Forehead of the Sky). Chomolungma is the Tibetan name.

text: In a certain code 'CAT' is written as 'DDY'. How is 'BIG' written?
Statements: All bags are handles. All handles are clips. Conclusion: I. All bags are clips. II. All clips are bags.
explanation: If A is inside B, and B is inside C, then A is inside C (All A are C). But C is not necessarily inside A.

text: If 1st January 2001 was Monday, what day was it on 1st January 2002?
explanation: 2001 is a normal year (365 days = 1 odd day). Monday + 1 = Tuesday.

text: Find the next number: 10, 20, 31, 43, 56, ?
explanation: Differences are +10, +11, +12, +13. Next is +14. 56 + 14 = 70.

text: Which is the highest waterfall in India?
explanation: Kunchikal Falls (Karnataka) is the highest tiered waterfall in India. Jog falls is the highest 'un-tiered' drop.

text: What is the pH value of pure water?
explanation: pH 7 is neutral; below 7 is acidic, above 7 is basic.

text: The 'Preamble' of the Indian Constitution was amended for the first time by which act?
explanation: The 42nd Amendment (1976) added 'Socialist', 'Secular', and 'Integrity' to the Preamble.

text: Who was the first Indian to fly into space?
explanation: Wing Commander Rakesh Sharma flew aboard Soyuz T-11 in 1984.

text: Which is the longest river in the world?
explanation: The Nile (Africa) is generally considered the longest. Amazon is the largest by volume.
